title: Autonomous regional escort fallback for pinned models
creator: Alex Rivera
description: Design and implement an autonomous fallback orchestrator that escorts traffic from pinned model versions to compatible alternatives across regions and model variants while preserving SLA guarantees and minimizing quality regression. This work touches routing policy, perf profile publishing, deprecation propagation, and Console visibility.
background: Customers frequently pin model versions for stability. When a pinned version becomes temporarily unavailable (hardware outage, hotfix rollout) or is scheduled for deprecation, current simple 'global fallback to latest' behavior causes cross-region surprises and unforeseen quality drop. We need region-aware, policy-driven escorting that prefers local compatible variants, respects pin contracts, and publishes clear deprecation signals to customers.
goals: Implement a deterministic, priority-ordered fallback decision engine that considers region, latency headroom, cost tier, and model performance profile
Expose a per-pin fallback policy that can be set by customers (strict, best-effort, regional-only, allow-variant-upgrade)
Ensure deprecation signals are propagated to Console and API warnings with an automated migration path suggestion
Maintain observability: per-request fallback reason, time-of-fallback, and quality-estimate delta in tracing and cost dashboards
non_goals: Full auto-upgrade of pinned production traffic without explicit customer opt-in
Rewriting the entire routing stack in this ticket (we will add a decision layer that plugs into routing)
acceptance_criteria: Traffic routed away from a pinned version in region A must follow the configured fallback policy
Fallback chain must include at least two alternative variants before stepping to cross-region options
Console shows deprecation banner and recommended migration (model + quantization) when server signals deprecation
No customer-level SLA regression for P1 customers during orchestrated fallback > 99.9% of the time in synthetic tests
implementation_notes: Add a 'fallback policy' table to the control plane (policy is small: tier, prefer_local, allow_variant_upgrade, fallback_timeout_ms). When a candidate request fails or node pool is saturated, the decision layer evaluates local-variant candidates using published perf profiles (latency-percentiles, memory footprint) and selects the highest-scoring compatible target. If none match, escalate to cross-region candidates respecting data residency tags.
tradeoffs: Stricter policies (strict pin) guarantee quality but increase error surface and latency spikes during partial outages. Best-effort policies lower errors at cost of possible quality regression. Implementing optimistic cross-region routing improves availability but may violate residency constraints; therefore we require an explicit customer flag to allow cross-region fallback.
progress_updates: 2025-01-27: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Routing, Console, and Product. Agreed on high-level API for fallback policy and required perf profile fields.
2025-02-03: Prototype decision layer implemented in an isolated service. Integration tests added to evaluate local vs cross-region selection heuristics.
2025-02-09: Added Console mockups for deprecation banners and per-pin policy UI. Design review scheduled.
2025-02-12: Benchmarked candidate selection latency; decision layer adds median 2ms overhead under normal load, 12ms under extreme pathing (acceptable).
decisions: Use published performance profiles (p50/p95 latencies, max memory) as primary compatibility filters rather than model name heuristics
Fallback policy defaults to 'regional-prefer' (prefer local compatible variants, then cross-region as last resort).
Deprecation state will be a first-class signal surfaced in the model catalog with a 'recommended replacement' UID. Console will show migration guidance and scheduled deprecation date.
Do not auto-upgrade pinned customers without opt-in; instead provide canary migration tools and a one-click 'accept fallback' flow in Console for admins.
risks: Quality regression if perf profiles are stale — require profile publishing as part of onboarding and add a profile staleness check
Incorrect residency handling could expose data across regions — add strict tag validation and explicit opt-in for cross-region fallbacks
Complexity in rollout: orchestrator bugs could route traffic incorrectly; we will gate behind feature flag and run canaries
tasks: Control plane: schema change to store fallback policies and deprecation metadata (ENG-42191)
Runtime: decision layer integration and policy enforcement in request path (ENG-42202)
Console: UI for per-pin fallback policy and deprecation banners (DES-1345)
Routing: coordinate region-residency checks and capacity signals (ENG-41900)
E2E tests: synthetic workload testing and SLO validation across regions (ENG-42310)
notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the perf-profile fields required by the decision layer; small missing fields will force conservative fallbacks. We will require an ops playbook for emergency pin overrides and a migration runbook for Enterprise customers.
